A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PEP-FedPT and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Corresponding methods, experiments, and proofs can be matched despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original federated-learning experiments on four datasets, including benchmark comparisons, held-out evaluations, ablations, privacy-noise experiments, and convergence analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results and adds client-percentile evaluations, heterogeneity and temperature sensitivity experiments, and prompt-evolution analyses.

M1.justification: The core CCMP mixing, prompt architecture, and federated optimization remain unchanged. However, Section A.4.1 revises the optional privacy procedure from noise applied during server updates to client-side noise before prototype transmission, with client-indexed sensitivity and sample counts. The new overview pseudocode does not introduce another core algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same classification tasks on CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet, DomainNet, and federated iNaturalist. The added Dirichlet concentrations vary partitions within existing coverage; they do not introduce another dataset, domain, or task.

E2.justification: V2 withdraws pFedPG's numerical held-out comparisons, replacing them with NA in Table 3 and Table 14, corresponding to v1 Table 13. Its participating-client results remain. Other comparator membership is retained; the newly cited domain-generalization methods are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The iNaturalist worst-accuracy metric changes from the minimum accuracy over the final 250 rounds, specified in v1's appendix footnote, to the 15th percentile of client accuracies. V2 additionally evaluates 5th and 10th percentiles, Dirichlet concentrations 0.1 and 0.5, temperature sweeps, and a temperature-by-insertion-layer grid. These substantially extend the evaluation design while retaining the principal training budgets.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component, prior, prompt-count, and placement ablations, v2 adds lower-tail client analysis, heterogeneity sensitivity, temperature sensitivity, temperature-placement interactions, and prompt evolution across rounds 0, 10, and 20. These address several previously untested robustness and mechanism questions. Figure 11 mainly redisplays existing held-out results.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three repetitions and report mean and standard deviation. V1 calls these different initializations and v2 calls them different runs, without stating a changed repetition count or uncertainty procedure. Additional result rows reuse the existing reporting convention.

E6.justification: Most principal scores remain unchanged, but Tables 15–17 and Figure 10 add substantial results. At Dir(0.5), PEP-FedPT reports 87.75±0.04 mean accuracy versus FedVPT-D's 87.92±0.74. Its iNaturalist worst entry changes from 57.61±0.82 to 41.10±0.48 under a different metric, not a comparable performance decline. Four pFedPG held-out entries become NA. Figure 8's weights change, and Figure 6 replaces the Tiny-ImageNet convergence curves with curves matching CIFAR-100 Figure 3 despite retaining its Tiny-ImageNet caption.

T1.justification: V2 adds a sensitivity-bound derivation claiming differential privacy in Section A.4.1 and formally constructs the representation distribution as a pushforward measure in Section A.6.2. Section A.6.3 changes the convergence bound's denominator from sqrt(RLS) to sqrt(TLS). The central quadratic-bound and MMSE propositions and most proofs remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: personalization through globally shared prompts, prototype-and-prior-based mixing, quadratic-bound and MMSE interpretations, and strong benchmark performance. Added evidence and explanatory wording do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands qualifications concerning long-tailed classes, IID conditions, and the shared-minimizer assumption's applicability to feature heterogeneity. It explains temperature-dependent placement behavior and explicitly cautions against interpreting pFedPG's unsuitable zero-shot evaluation as its general effectiveness. The privacy discussion also advances from empirical noise tolerance to an explicit privacy-guarantee claim.

D1.justification: New Table 7 consolidates previously scattered settings and newly specifies a ten-round centroid-update interval and 1% iNaturalist participation. These improve documentation without establishing changes to the retained experiments. The main optimizer, learning rate, hardware, training budgets, and prompt settings remain documented as before.

R1.justification: V2 adds brief positioning relative to FedSR, GA, FedGaLA, and prompt-based domain adaptation by Jin et al. It also adds FedProto and Dwork–Roth references supporting prototype sharing and privacy. The principal positioning against existing federated prompt-tuning methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The overall section structure and much wording remain intact. Local revisions expand the introduction and method explanations, add an overview pseudocode, clarify assumptions, correct references, and extend appendix subsections. These are targeted editorial and structural changes rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: V2 adds settings and analysis tables, temperature and prompt-evolution plots, and a personalization/generalization display. It redraws existing diagnostic figures, changes axes and legends, and places Table 6 beside Figure 3. Figure 11 replots existing results, while the original training-loss Figure 10 becomes Figure 13; these are distinguished from genuinely added displays.

improvement.justification: The sensitivity experiments, meaningful client-percentile evaluation, clearer settings, and qualified pFedPG comparison modestly strengthen support for the unchanged central results. Material drawbacks limit the gain: Figure 6 now duplicates CIFAR-100 curves under a Tiny-ImageNet caption, and the new privacy argument does not establish that its empirical sensitivity estimate bounds all neighboring datasets. The added evidence and clearer applicability boundaries nevertheless provide a limited net improvement.
